# pii


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Personal information, often called PII, is text that identifies a person
or opens one of their accounts: an email address, a phone number, a card
or bank account number, a national identity number such as a UK National
Insurance number or an Indian Aadhaar number, a street address, a date
of birth, an API key or password. The detector is a separate package,
[rahasya](https://vedicreader.github.io/rahasya/). It works with
patterns and checksums rather than a model. A card number has to pass
the Luhn check and an NHS number its mod-11 check, so the detector gives
the same answer every time and downloads nothing. On a held-out test set
of 240 generated documents it missed nothing and raised no false alarm
(`evals/RESULTS.md`, section 3).

Names are the gap. No pattern describes a name, so name detection is a
second pass, and it finds only a name that follows a title such as Mr,
Dr or Prof: “Dr Charles Babbage” is found, “Ada Lovelace” on her own is
not. The pass runs when a document is added (except on code, where
identifiers are not names) and by default in `ask`;
[`Vault.pii`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/pii.html#vault.pii)
and [`gated`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/pii.html#gated)
run it only with `ner=True`. When a document holds personal information
the detector cannot see, a person marks it, as below.

This page is the half of the work that needs a vault: the marks a person
sets, the privacy level of each document, the table of findings, and
[`gated`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/pii.html#gated),
which applies a policy to what search and reading return. What `ask` and
the other model calls send to a model is on [ask](02_ask.ipynb).

## Checking a document, and gating retrieval

`Vault.pii(ref)` answers for one whole document: whether it holds
personal information, which kinds, and whether a person’s mark overrides
the detector. `detected` is the detector’s own verdict and `override` is
the mark. `mark_pii` marks a document as personal when the detector
finds nothing, for example a letter that names people without titles.
`mark_not_pii` clears a false alarm, such as your own invoice, and only
a person may set it (see the next section).
[`pii_ctx`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/pii.html#pii_ctx)
runs the detector over every section of an assembled context, the result
of `context`, which is what `ask` decides on.

Retrieval is the other half. `search`, `sections`, `context`, `read`,
`document`, `toc`, `doc_context` and `federate` all take `pii=`, which
says what happens to a row that holds personal information:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>pii=</code></th>
<th>the row’s text becomes</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>off</code>, the default in Python and the CLI</td>
<td>the stored text; nothing is checked</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>redact</code></td>
<td>the stored text with each recognised identifier replaced by its
kind, as in <code>[EMAIL]</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>refuse</code></td>
<td>a placeholder such as
<code>[withheld: personal information (card, email)]</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Under `redact` and `refuse` the row stays in the results, its title and
breadcrumb are masked rather than removed, and a `pii` key names the
kinds found, so a caller can still say why something was held back.
Three cases follow from the levels below. A Local only document is
withheld under `redact` as well as `refuse`, and so are its title,
breadcrumb and source. A document that is private only because of a mark
or the shelf’s floor, with nothing the detector recognises, passes
through `redact` unchanged, because there is nothing to mask; use
`refuse` when that matters. A document a person cleared with
`mark_not_pii` comes back untouched, unless the shelf’s floor is above
Open.

The [MCP server](05_mcp.ipynb) hands its results to a model the vault
does not run, so there every tool defaults to `redact`, and every result
is gated whatever the tool, including `ask`’s. A client may ask for
`refuse`. It may not ask for `off`.

## Learned detectors were measured and not shipped

Two learned PII models, an ONNX build and a TFLite build, were tried
against the patterns. Both were worse on precision and on recall, and
about 200 times slower, so the shipped detector is the patterns alone.
The model code stays in `evals/backends.py`, `evals/pii_model.py` reruns
the comparison, and `evals/RESULTS.md` has the numbers.

## Privacy levels and findings

Every document has one of three privacy levels. The level decides what
this package’s own model calls may send to a model that runs somewhere
other than this machine, called a hosted model below.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>level</th>
<th>how a document gets it</th>
<th>what a hosted model may be sent</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Open (<code>open</code>)</td>
<td>nothing personal found, or a person cleared it</td>
<td>the text as it is</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Personal (<code>personal</code>)</td>
<td>the detector found an identifier, or someone marked it</td>
<td>it depends on the policy: masked text, nothing, or with
<code>allow=True</code> the whole text (see <a
href="02_ask.ipynb">ask</a>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Local only (<code>local</code>)</td>
<td>someone set it with <code>set_level</code>, or its type is
sensitive</td>
<td>nothing; only a model on this machine reads it</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The sensitive types come from
[varga](https://vedicreader.github.io/varga/): passport, ID card, bank
statement, payslip, tax return and clinical record. These rules cover
what vishalakshi sends to models. In Python and the CLI they do not stop
retrieval: `read` or `search` with the default `pii='off'` still returns
a Local only document’s text to whoever called it. The MCP server
defaults to `redact`, which withholds it.

`level(ref)` works a document’s level out in three steps. A mark set
with `mark_pii`, `mark_not_pii` or `set_level`, if there is one,
decides. Otherwise the level is the higher of the type’s level and the
findings’ level, where any identifier found in its text or its title
makes it Personal. Finally the result is raised to the shelf’s floor.
The floor is a level no document on the shelf can go below, set with
`set_floor`. A shelf for medical records can have a floor of Local only,
so a new document there is protected before anything has been detected
in it. `level(ref, page=n)` gives one page’s level from that page’s
findings; a page with no text takes the whole document’s level.

Raising a level is always allowed. Lowering one is not. `set_level` to a
lower level, removing a mark, `mark_not_pii`, `reject_pii`, `reset_pii`
and lowering a floor all take `by=` and raise `PermissionError` unless
`by='person'`. The default is `'person'`, so a person’s own code passes
nothing, and an agent passes its own name. The [MCP
server](05_mcp.ipynb) does not offer `by`, so a model client cannot
claim to be a person, and it cannot turn the retrieval gate off with
`pii='off'` either.

When a document is added, `scan_pii` scans each page and files every
identifier in the `pii_findings` table as a finding: its kind, its page,
its start and end offsets in the page text, and a fingerprint. The
fingerprint is a 16-character hash of the kind and the value with
spacing, dashes and case removed, so `ADA@example.com` and
`ada@example.com`, or `4111-1111-1111-1111` and `4111 1111 1111 1111`,
give the same fingerprint. The table does not hold the value. The value
is still in the document’s text, which the vault keeps as it was read,
and the hash has no secret key, so a short value such as a date of birth
could be recovered by hashing every possible one. Treat the findings
table as exactly as private as the vault file. `findings` lists them,
each with a masked preview such as `a••@e••••••.com` taken from the
current page text.

A person can give a verdict on a finding. `accept_pii` confirms it is
personal, which an agent may also do, since it can only raise a level.
`reject_pii` says it is not, and the level falls if nothing else holds
it up. `reset_pii` takes a verdict back. A verdict is stored against the
fingerprint, so it covers every occurrence of the same value in the
document and it survives the page being read again: the new findings get
new ids and keep the old verdict. A finding id from before the re-read
comes back as `stale`.
